label: Using Unity for modding
title: Using Unity for modding
lead: Use the guided CU authoring lane for bundled minigame screens and body animation curves without living inside the whole ripped project.
bodyHtml:
What this workflow is for

This lane is intentionally narrow for CUCoreLib v1: bundled minigame screen prefabs and bundled body curve assets only.

Do not use this path for generic scene export, items, buildings, locale, recipes, or other systems. Export only the minimum surface needed for one bundle registration path.

The goal is to give you one controlled lane so you can author the asset, export the bundle, copy a matching runtime snippet, and return to normal C# mod code.

Project and editor version

Open CU Mod Project/CU Mod Project in Unity 2022.3.62f3. That project already contains the ripped game content plus the new Assets/CU Authoring workspace.

This lane is intentionally narrow: bundle screens and body curve assets only. Everything else should stay in normal C# modding workflows.

From there, use Tools > CU Modding > Authoring Hub. That is the supported entry point for this workflow. Ignore ThunderKit here.

Video slot: opening the Unity project and the Authoring Hub.

The golden path

  1. Open Tools > CU Modding > Authoring Hub.
  2. Enter a pack name such as WireSplice.
  3. Click Create Starter Pack.
  4. Edit the generated assets under Assets/CU Authoring/User Assets/<PackName>.
  5. Click Validate until the bundle is clean.
  6. Click Export.
  7. Optional: set Target plugin folder and click Install Exported Bundle into Target.
  8. Click Copy Snippet and paste the result into your mod.
  9. Call your registered path in runtime code and confirm it resolves without null refs.

The starter pack creates a bundle profile, a blank minigame screen prefab, one AnimationCurveAsset, and one BodyAnimationCurveProfileAsset.

That is the only required end-to-end output contract for CUCoreLib v1 authoring.

Video slot: full create -> validate -> export -> copy snippet flow.

Authoring minigame screens

Use New Blank Minigame Screen when you want a clean screen prefab that CUCoreLib can mount under the live minigame UI. The root should stay a RectTransform, and the prefab should not contain its own Canvas or EventSystem.

Use Clone Vanilla Screen when you want reference material from vanilla screens like BandageMinigame or SyringeMinigame. Treat those clones as study aids first. They usually need cleanup before export because the validator blocks ripped-game sprite, audio, and prefab dependencies.

public override void Start(CUCoreMinigameSession session)
{
    session.TryCreateBundledScreen("wiresplice.minigames", "WireSpliceScreen");
}

Video slot: making a blank screen and cleaning a cloned vanilla screen.

Authoring body curves

Create an AnimationCurveAsset when you want one reusable curve. Create a BodyAnimationCurveProfileAsset when you want one asset that points at several named curves for several body fields.

The custom profile inspector lets you pick real curve assets instead of typing asset names by hand. That matters because CUCoreLib resolves bundled curves by asset name.

BodyAnimationCurves.TryApplyBundledProfile(body, "wiresplice.minigames", "WireSpliceProfile");

Video slot: editing a curve and filling out a profile asset.

What validation checks

The validator keeps this workflow narrow on purpose. If it stops you, it is usually protecting you from a bundle that only worked because it was still leaning on the ripped project.

CheckWhy it matters
Root must be a RectTransformBundled minigame screens are mounted into the live minigame canvas.
No Canvas or EventSystem in the screen prefabThe game already owns those UI systems.
Assets must live under Assets/CU AuthoringThis keeps the supported workspace separate from the rest of the ripped project.
No ripped-game dependencies in authored exportsReference-only clones are convenient, but they are not a safe final export target.
No blank or stale profile AssetName entriesCurve bundles resolve by exported asset name.

Where export goes

Export writes bundles to CUCoreExports/Bundles/<BundleFileName> at the Unity project root.

Use Install Exported Bundle into Target to copy the bundle (and manifest) into your plugin's Bundles/ folder, then register it in code.

private void Awake()
{
    AssetLoader.RegisterBundleFromPluginFolder(this, "wiresplice.minigames", "Bundles/wiresplice-minigames");
}
// Runtime options:
session.TryCreateBundledScreen("wiresplice.minigames", "WireSpliceScreen");
session.TryCreateScreen("cclbundle://wiresplice.minigames/WireSpliceScreen");

Use whichever screen path is clearer for your codebase; both resolve through the same CUCoreLib bundle path registration.

Video slot: showing the export output folder and moving the bundle into a mod.

Migration / recovery path

  1. Restore the expected folder layout under Assets/CU Authoring.
  2. Close Unity, delete Library/ and Temp/.
  3. Reopen Unity and let it reimport.
  4. Re-export one sample bundle before moving on to broader changes.

One-command smoke check

From a clean authoring session: create a starter pack, build and validate it, export, install into a test mod plugin folder, and call:

session.TryCreateScreen("cclbundle://wiresplice.minigames/WireSpliceScreen");
BodyAnimationCurves.TryApplyBundledProfile(body, "wiresplice.minigames", "WireSpliceProfile");

If the call succeeds and the screen appears, your bundle contract matches the CUCoreLib runtime boundary.

Keep the scope narrow

Use this Unity workflow for bundled minigame screen prefabs and bundled body curve data. Do not treat it as the main path for items, buildings, locale, recipes, or other normal CUCoreLib registration work.

If all you need is the runtime minigame class, stay in C# and use the Minigames page. Reach for Unity only when the visual screen or bundled curve asset is the thing you actually need to author.

Next pages

Once your bundle exists, jump to Minigames for the runtime screen-loading side and Loading assets for the current AssetBundle scope and runtime caveats.

If your mod project is not building yet, go back to Setup first and make sure your BepInEx DLL is healthy before you spend time in Unity.
